title: Cross-SDK: recommended retry envelope, idempotency token format, and stream-resume ergonomics
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: define a pragmatic, cross-language defaults and developer ergonomics spec for (1) retry/backoff envelope, (2) idempotency key format and lifetime guidance, and (3) streaming resume semantics for partial responses. This ticket scopes the API contract and sample patterns for Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs so product surfaces behave consistently and are easy for engineers to adopt. The aim is to reduce customer confusion, prevent accidental double side-effects, and make streaming robust in transient-failure scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A short, implementable spec exists that each SDK can follow: default retryable error taxonomy, default exponential backoff parameters, idempotency key format + recommended placement, and stream-resume APIs for partial transcripts. 2) Language SDKs include examples (sync+async) demonstrating: creating idempotency tokens, passing them, and recovering from retries; streaming with a resume token; and a canonical test harness that validates no duplicate side-effects for common server behaviors. 3) Docs and one cross-SDK sample app (chat bot) are published in the SDK repo and referenced in Console docs. 4) Security review completed for idempotency token storage patterns (client and server).
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Draft spec (this ticket) with explicit examples for Python, TS, Go. Phase 2: Implement minimal API primitives in each SDK: - RetryPolicy class/config with language idioms - IdempotencyKey helper (generator + encoder) - StreamResumeToken type and resume(stream_id, token) helper. Phase 3: Add tests and integration harness that simulates server transient errors and verifies exactly-once semantics where possible. Phase 4: Docs, samples, and internal rollout. Timeline: 2 sprints to land spec + prototypes; SDK implementations in subsequent sprint. Owner: SDK Platform team; reviewers: Runtime, Product, Security, Console docs.
compatibility_notes: Defaults are intentionally conservative to avoid breaking existing customers: retriable errors limited to network timeouts, 429, and 5xx except 501/505. Backoff defaults: initial=50ms, multiplier=2.0, max_delay=2s, max_attempts=4. These can be overridden by users. Idempotency token format: opaque base64url-safe string with an optional structured prefix for server routing (e.g., rdw:v1:ctx:<base64>), but SDKs should not try to parse payloads—servers can. Stream resume will be opt-in: server must emit resume_token in-stream; SDKs expose resume(token) API. We avoid automatic resume-on-error unless caller enables it.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: customers may assume stronger exactly-once guarantees than the platform provides; Mitigation: doc warnings, examples showing when duplicate side effects are possible and recommended server-side guards (idempotency db token check, conditional writes). Risk: exposing structured idempotency tokens might tempt clients to include sensitive payloads; Mitigation: recommend opaque tokens and provide server-side canonical encoders for callers that need server-side routing. Risk: stream resume complexity across languages; Mitigation: keep a small, language-idiomatic surface: resume(token) and on_resume_failed callback.
testing_plan: Unit tests for SDK helpers (token generation/validation), deterministic backoff math tests, and mocks for network failure scenarios. Integration test: deploy a toy runtime that simulates transient 'partial write' failure patterns and ensures SDK retry behavior + idempotency tokens prevent duplicate side-effects in >=95% of cases. End-to-end sample app (chat) run in CI that exercises stream resume flow: start stream, server emits resume_token, simulate connection drop, resume and assert continuity and no duplicate user-visible messages.

comments: 2025-11-04 Maya Chen: Initial draft created after cross-team sync. Key open questions: token lifetime, whether SDKs should rotate tokens automatically, and whether resume tokens should be JWT-like or opaque.

2025-11-06 Rafael Ortiz: Added pragmatic backoff defaults based on telemetry from hosted API (median retryable latency ~60ms). Suggested reducing max_attempts to 3 for mobile-focused SDKs—left as overrideable in config.

2025-11-10 Anika Patel (Security): Flagged that client-side token generators must not embed PHI or user secrets. Added recommendation to mark token generators as non-deterministic and to provide server-side token creation endpoints for regulated customers.
2025-11-12 Luke Kramer (Runtime): Server will emit resume_token as base64url and will accept it via resume endpoint /streams/<id>/resume with POST {token}. We will keep token opaque to SDKs.
2025-11-15 Rafael Ortiz: Pushed prototype helper APIs to python/ts/go SDK branches. See prototype PRs linked above. Need review for ergonomics and naming (RetryPolicy vs RetryConfig).
2025-11-17 Product review: PM requested a simple one-line example for docs showing how to call resume and how to pass idempotency key in request headers. Added to docs task list.
2025-11-18 Maya Chen: Updated acceptance criteria to require security review result. Ready for formal review; requesting sign-off from Runtime and Security.
